dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the empty-paths early return in content_matches_main cannot mislabel a non-ancestor branch as MERGED-REBASED without a positive liveness signal that a real comparison ran.
evidence: infra/gerrit/feature-branch-inventory.sh:51: 	paths="$(git diff --name-only "${main_sha}...${rev}" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
infra/gerrit/feature-branch-inventory.sh:52: 	[ -z "$paths" ] && return 0

Litmus: the `return 0` (matches) verdict is produced when the producer emitted nothing, so the check cannot distinguish 'touched files all match main' from 'diff produced no paths' — it fails open toward MERGED-REBASED.
infra/gerrit/feature-branch-inventory.sh:60: 	git diff --quiet "$main_sha" "$rev" -- "$@" 2>/dev/null
infra/gerrit/feature-branch-inventory.sh:63: main_sha="$(git ls-remote "https://${GERRIT_USER}@${GERRIT_HOST}/a/${PROJECT}" refs/heads/main | awk '{print $1}')"
search_files for 'git fetch' in the script returned (no matches) — the revs/main_sha are never fetched into the local repo before local diff/merge-base run.
ABSENCE: no check that `git cat-file -e $rev` / `$main_sha` succeeds before the local comparisons, so a missing-object error is silently collapsed into a classification verdict.
dropped.finding: content_matches_main returns success (0 => MERGED-REBASED) when `git diff --name-only` yields empty output, but an empty result is indistinguishable from a real content match: it occurs both when the branch truly touched nothing since merge-base and when the diff simply emitted nothing (e.g. a degenerate/whitespace-only diff or a rev whose tree resolves oddly). A non-ancestor branch that produces empty name-only output is silently reported as landed/MERGED-REBASED.
merged_from: Neither content_matches_main nor the merge-base check asserts that main_sha and the branch rev are present as LOCAL git objects. main_sha comes from `git ls-remote` and revs come from the Gerrit REST API; the script never fetches them. If the objects are absent locally, `git diff`/`git merge-base` error, but the errors are suppressed with 2>/dev/null and mapped to a definite classification (NOT-IN-MAIN, or content 'no match'), so 'the objects were not available to compare' is indistinguishable from 'checked and genuinely differs'.
scenarios: A feature branch that is not an ancestor of main and whose three-dot name-only diff is empty is labelled MERGED-REBASED rather than NOT-IN-MAIN.
